alerts.detail: ONE. Scanned last run, not this run. ecomm.one-line.com/one-ecom/schedule/routing-finder redirects to /one-ecom/static/maintenance/global/index.html reading "eCommerce Temporarily Unavailable ... an unexpected technical issue". Site-wide outage, not the per-session "Thanks for Your Patience" ceiling. Premier Alliance EC1-EC4, Yang Ming and HMM tonnage is normally seen only through ONE, so that tonnage is uncovered this run.

CMA CGM. Not retrievable: cma-cgm.com/ebusiness/schedules serves a planned-maintenance notice for 12 Sep 17:00 CEST to 13 Sep 05:00 CEST and this run fell inside it. Distinct from the DataDome 403 recorded on previous runs. No POST quota was consumed and none was shared with liner-tracker-market-refresh, so the next run should reach the routing finder normally.

MSC and ZIM. Blocked on 11 and 12 Sep with SearchSailingRoutes answering 200 and an empty body. Cause found: the endpoint needs MSC internal integer port ids, and a bare scripted POST still returns an empty Data array even with the right ids and body shape. Working method: load msc.com/en/search-a-schedule, take the Alpine component that owns searchPointToPoint, set selectedPortFrom / selectedPortTo to entries from its own searchCountryPortResults array (580 ports, each with PortId and LocationCode) and selectedDate, then await searchPointToPoint() and read results off the sibling component. Service name is results[i].MaritimeService.label, lower case. RoutingType is the Direct / Transhipment flag. Eight lanes scanned this way with no unknown service strings.

Lanes not covered this run: all CMA CGM lanes; all ONE lanes; Evergreen CNSHA-USSAV, CNNGB-USSAV, CNNGB-USHOU, KRPUS-USSAV, KRPUS-USHOU, VNTOT-USSAV, VNTOT-USHOU, CNTAO-USNYC and CNXMN-USNYC; Hapag CNSHA-USSAV, CNNGB-USSAV, CNNGB-USHOU, KRPUS-USSAV, VNVUT-USSAV and VNVUT-USHOU; Maersk KRPUS-USEWR, KRPUS-USSAV, CNNGB-USSAV, CNNGB-USHOU, VNVUT-USSAV and VNVUT-USHOU; MSC CNSHA-USSAV, CNNGB-USSAV, CNNGB-USHOU, KRPUS-USSAV, KRPUS-USHOU, VNVUT-USSAV and VNVUT-USHOU. In addition, Evergreen weeks 42 to 44 are not covered at all because Evergreen publishes only about four weeks ahead.

No first sighting this run. All three published items reappeared with identical dates, so there is no EXTRA LOADER DETECTED, no EXTRA LOADER UPDATED and no EXTRA LOADER GONE. Detector fixtures both passed: Hapag CNYTN-USNYC returned AA7 5 with isGemini false and US4 6 with isGemini true and flagged nothing, and Evergreen CNSHA-USNYC returned SAX 5, NUE2 4, CBX 3, NUE 2 and OGEC 1 and flagged OGEC only.

OGME added to ignoredCodes. Evergreen runs a second ad-hoc programme labelled "Ocean-Going Ad Hoc call Middle East(OGME)", seen on EVER LUCKY 0012-084W and 0012-084E routing Qingdao / Shanghai / Ningbo / Kaohsiung / Shekou / Singapore to Khor Fakkan. It matches the ad-hoc label regex and would publish as a false positive on any lane that touches the Middle East, but it is a different trade and never calls USNYC, USSAV or USHOU. AUG was checked and is already in the registry, correctly: the carrier string is "Asia-U.S. GULF Service(AUG)" with a full westbound return leg, so it is a proforma Gulf service, not an extra loader.

Method changes worth keeping. 1) Evergreen can be driven with no autocomplete seed at all: setting tvs2OriAC_hideValue and tvs2DesAC_hideValue, calling checkACViaUSCA on both and then frmSubmit works from a cold page load. 2) ShipmentLink drops the connection with ERR_CONNECTION_CLOSED after roughly six searches in quick succession; a 20 second pause clears it and the session continues. 3) Maersk geo ids can be resolved without the UI from api.maersk.com/synergy/reference-data/geography/locations with the Consumer-Key header taken from a captured routings-queries call; the field is maerskGeoLocationId and USNYC must be swapped for USEWR. 4) Wrapping window.fetch twice in one page session causes unbounded recursion and silently breaks the site own requests; restore a clean fetch from a hidden same-origin iframe before driving a page component.
